The shared services center moved to another city. Any payroll question now goes through a trilingual ticket. Your colleague is crying over the form. Help?
In the morning floor chat, 700 people argue about the hallway windows. Someone tags you as "the floor's old-timer." Weigh in?
The next team grabs "your" window desks every morning because they arrive 10 minutes earlier. Your team is annoyed. How do you solve it?
Colleagues from a regional branch are visiting HQ and are lost. You meet them in the lobby at 8:40. Your meeting's at 9. Give them a tour?
In the morning you learn a colleague has a milestone birthday, and nobody signed a card or ordered a cake. He just walked in. What do you do?
Your counterpart in another time zone hands over work at 7 a.m. your time daily. Today, nothing, and he's not answering. What do you do?
Your co-presenter is late for a pitch to a VP. He texts: "Start without me, I'm in the elevator." The elevator takes ten minutes to reach 40. Start?
Some of your team's work is being outsourced abroad. The team fears being replaced. You're asked to train the contractors. Do it?
right: Train them, but talk to your team

text: An IT colleague invites you to lunch "just because." You barely know him, but you'll need his help next week. Go?
Two of your people are fighting in the department chat in front of 300 people. The department head has already reacted with the eyes emoji. Step in?
In a meeting, the head of another team presents your idea as his own. Your team is watching you. What do you do?
Five interns follow you all day because "that's what the internship program says." You head to the restroom — so do they. What do you do?
left: Give them a task and space

text: An Accounting colleague asks for help with her deck: "You're good at making things pretty." You are, but you have three of your own. Help?
On a call, a colleague from a distant branch admits no one at HQ has answered her emails for a month. You could help. Take it on?
At the water cooler, people say your boss is leaving and you're tipped to replace him. You know nothing. Fan the rumor?
A new hire emailed all 40,000 employees asking, "Where's the restroom?" Thousands of "unsubscribe me" replies pour in. He's pale. What do you do?
Your team and Marketing are fighting over a shared events budget. Marketing proposes peace: "Half each, but you organize." Agree?
Your team has worked until 8 p.m. for three weeks. At stand-up, everyone stares at the table. Have a heart-to-heart?
right: Promise time off after the project

text: You find a colleague in tears in the meeting room. Your client meeting there starts in five minutes. What do you do?
In the evening the team votes in chat on Friday plans: karaoke or an escape room. You hate both. Vote?
A colleague you've worked with for seven years tells you in the evening he's leaving for another company. He asks you to keep it quiet until Monday. Your reaction?
right: Try to talk him out of it

text: A colleague texts at 9 p.m.: "Can you cover my shift tomorrow? My kid has a school play." You have your own plans. Agree?
After a hard day, the team suggests ordering pizza and hanging out at the office. You've been dreaming of your couch. Stay an hour?
In the evening a colleague sends an 11-minute voice message. It begins: "So, real quick." Listen?
Your former team invites you to a department reunion tonight. Your current team is celebrating a launch at the same time. Where do you go?
A colleague confides she's job hunting and asks you for a reference. Your boss asked to be told about such things. What do you do?
right: Suggest she talk to the boss

text: The night support shift asks you to hop on a call: "Five minutes, we need your expertise." It's 11:30 p.m. Join?
right: Ask them to write it up

text: New policy: three office days a week, tracked by turnstile. It's Tuesday, a plumber's at home and you have calls all day. Go in?
You wake up with a fever. An e-sick note needs approval from your manager, HR and the "absence coordinator," who replies by 11. What do you do?
right: Go back to bed, notify everyone

text: You need a photo for your new badge. The photographer takes one shot, "per policy." You blinked. A retake requires a request. Keep it?
The corporate university enrolled you in "Strategic Thinking" every morning at 7:30 for a month. Opting out needs a memo to the rector. Go?
Free corporate English — Wednesdays at 8 a.m. The teacher asks you to describe your job. You realize you can't explain it in your own language either. Try?
left: Give it a go in English

text: New policy: every document needs a label — Public, Internal, Confidential or Restricted. Your shopping list is in a shared folder. What label?
A new quota: 50 pages per person per month. Your board report is 80 pages and must be on paper. What do you do?
A colleague is going on parental leave, and her duties are being divvied up. You get three projects and her cactus. Handover at 9. What do you do?
New flex-time program: start anytime from 7 to 11 a.m. You choose 11. Your boss arrives at 7 and stares at your empty desk. What do you do?
Remote policy allows working "from anywhere with reliable internet." You want a week at your country house. Internet works only in the attic. Go?
You bring a stack to the shredder, but it takes only five sheets at a time. The stack is 500 "Restricted" pages. What do you do?
left: Feed it five at a time

text: The data protection course says don't put client names in emails. Your entire job is emailing clients by name. What now?
After lunch you return to your hot desk to find someone there eating your yogurt, having mixed up the shelf. What do you do?
New eco policy bans disposable cups. Bring your own mug. Yours is at home. You need coffee right now. What do you do?
The office installed five recycling bins. Your yogurt cup is made of three materials. The ESG team watches via cameras. Sort it?
HR needs a certificate stating you don't need a certificate. Without it, no vacation. Another department issues it in a week. What do you do?
right: Ask your boss for an exception

text: Sustainability wants your department's carbon footprint calculated. The method is 60 pages. You're the only one who read page one. Take it on?
A remote colleague in another city complains he misses the important "hallway" decisions. He's right. What do you do?
Working from home, at 7 p.m. it's unclear where work ends and evening begins. The laptop's still open on the kitchen table. Close it?
You're on sick leave, but in the evening your boss writes: "How are you? By the way, could you look at something?" It's an hour's work. Reply?
Evening homework for corporate English: an essay titled "My Company Values." By sentence three you realize it's satire. Hand it in?
On the evening subway, you see a coworker reading a "Restricted" document on his laptop. The person beside him is peeking. Say something?
On a date you're asked what you do. You say "I work at a big company" and realize your NDA stops you from saying more. How do you wriggle out?
A colleague on parental leave texts: "I miss work, what's new?" There's enough news for three reorgs. Tell her?
Friday evening: just you and the guard on the floor. He offers to switch off the lights "per eco policy" without waiting for you. Agree?
You promised the family no work tonight. While they watch a movie, you answer emails under a blanket. Your partner spots the phone glow. Confess?
Your kid needs a laptop for a school presentation tonight. Policy forbids using the work one. The home one's broken. What do you do?
left: Build it together on a phone

text: Morning announcement: the CEO will walk your floor at 10. The office manager asks you to clear personal items, including photos of your kids. Do it?
They repainted the walls overnight before the CEO's visit. The floor reeks of paint, and you're allergic. Work elsewhere?
You're summoned to the 52nd floor — executive level. Carpets, silence, and assistants eyeing your sneakers. You're in sneakers. Go as is?
The press office wants you to comment on an industry trend for a journalist. Your answer is pre-written: you're "confident in 40% growth." Say it?
right: Ask them to soften the number

text: The call center escalates a complaint: "Your contract is impossible to cancel." You check — it really is. Your reply?
The monthly sales target is 97% met. The boss suggests "topping up" with next month's deals. Your team objects. What do you do?
The CEO's assistant calls at 8:10: "He wants your deck in 20 minutes, printed, in color." The color printer is on 12. You're on 30. Run?
right: Ask to show it on screen

text: You learn two VPs are fighting over your project, each expecting your loyalty. Meeting with both at 11. How do you play it?
The CEO stops at your desk: "And what do you do?" Behind him your boss makes terrifying eyes. Your answer?
A trade journalist calls you directly asking for an "off-the-record comment." All press contact must go through the press office. What do you do?
A major client is yelling at one of your people on the phone. He's going pale. The script says "stay accommodating." Take over the call?
The CEO's assistant returns your report: "He only reads page one. Fit 40 pages onto one." In an hour. What do you do?
At an industry lunch you sit next to someone from a competitor. He sweetly asks about your plans. What do you share?
Sales promised a client a feature that doesn't exist. Due in a month. You find out after the fact. What do you do?
Someone from another department quietly offers an "alliance": back his project at committee, he'll back yours. His project is weak. Agree?
A client survey says they love your product but hate the 70-page contract. Legal opposes shortening it. Push for it?
The CEO is recording a welcome video and wants "real people in the background." You'd spend an hour pretending to work. You were picked. Agree?
left: Pretend to work for an hour

text: A key client calls at 9 p.m. to discuss "just a couple of things." He's 15% of revenue. Answer?
In the evening a VP's assistant asks you for a "short brief" for his morning meeting. It's on a topic you don't know. Take it on?
The evening news runs a story on your company. There you are, yawning in the background of the town hall. Friends are already sending screenshots. What do you do?
right: Ask the press office to swap it

text: In the evening you learn your team brought in record revenue. Only the boss got thanked. The team is upset. What do you do?
A call center rep DMs you after his shift: "Can I route difficult clients straight to you? You're the only one who helps." Agree?
A colleague whispers that the VP you backed lost out, and your project now belongs to his rival. Meeting the new sponsor tomorrow. Prep?
At 10 p.m. the press office sends your project's press release for approval. The dates are off by a year. It goes out at 8 a.m. Fix it?
right: Flag it and go to bed

text: At a family dinner a relative asks, "So, are you a director yet?" You've been a senior specialist for three years. Your answer?
Parking spots are now raffled monthly. You've lost five months running. A winning colleague who cycles offers to sell you his. Buy it?
The 40-space bike rack holds 120 bikes this morning. You chained yours to the entrance railing. Security threatens to cut the lock. What do you do?
left: Carry the bike into the office

text: After running to work, there's a line of six for the office shower, and only one showerhead works. Meeting in 25 minutes. Wait?
New system: lanyard color shows your grade. Yours is blue, interns green, directors gold. In the elevator everyone looks at lanyards. Hide yours?
You're handed a "10 Years With Us" pin. You've been here six. HR mixed you up with someone of the same surname. Say something?
The internal jobs portal offers you a six-month rotation in another department. New skills, but your project would lose you. Apply?
Pouring rain this morning. By the entrance, a stand: "Company umbrellas — take one, return one." It's been empty for six months. You're soaked. What do you do?
The office lost-and-found holds 300 chargers, 80 scarves and one guitar. You're looking for your charger. The clerk wants a description "per procedure." Describe it?
right: Grab a similar one and go

text: An outside partner is coming at 9. Guest registration requires 48 hours' notice. He's already at reception. What do you do?
left: Go down and meet him there

text: The nursing room is occupied: two salespeople are holding a meeting there "because there's nowhere else." A colleague with a baby waits at the door. Step in?
The company choir needs tenors for the anniversary show. The choir director heard you humming by the water cooler. Sign up?
Your department's football team is about to be relegated from the corporate league. They need a goalie. Last time you played goal was in school. Agree?
Translation Services translated your deck for the overseas office. "Profit" is rendered everywhere as "train arrival." You present in an hour. What do you do?
The floor kitchen's dishwasher has been full of other people's clean mugs for a week, and nobody unloads it. Your dirty mug waits in the sink. Who's going to do it?
The open space got soundproof phone booths: four for 500 people. A colleague has been in one for three hours, asleep. Wake him?
right: Take your call in the stairwell

text: In the company library you find a book called "How to Survive a Corporation," checked out 40 times. Every page is covered in colleagues' notes. Borrow it?
right: Leave it for those in need

text: You're offered three months at the overseas office. Exciting, but your kid starts first grade at home. Decide by end of day. What's your call?
Facilities introduces a plant policy: one pot per desk, max 30 cm. Your monstera is 1.2 meters, and the team adores it. What do you do?
In the evening a colleague retires after 38 years. He asks you to give the toast. You've known him for six months. Speak?
At the corporate chess club, you're paired with the CFO. He's losing and getting grim. Offer a draw next game?
You receive the company's New Year gift: last year's planner. Your kid asks what it is. How do you explain?
left: Give it to the kid to draw in

text: At the company gym, the VP on the next treadmill recognizes you and starts discussing the quarterly plan. You're mid-run. Keep talking?
On a trip abroad, local colleagues invite you to dinner at their home. You're tired, and you have an 8 a.m. meeting. Go?
At the company evening party there's a prize draw. You win a year's pool pass; a colleague wins a kettle. She really wants the pool. Swap?
7:50 p.m. The twelfth and final sign-off on your project belongs to a department where everyone's gone except the cleaner. She saw your document "on some desk." Search together?
Your vacation is finally approved — at 10 p.m. the night before your flight. But the order has the wrong date: starting tomorrow, last year. Fly?
left: Fly and sort it out later

text: The canteen launches "dinners for late workers," 7 to 9 p.m. Free food, but showing up means admitting you stayed late again. Go?
The global town hall starts at 11 p.m. your time. Viewing is logged toward your "engagement index." Watch live?
At 8:15 p.m. Legal returns your email with 87 tracked changes. The email is three lines long. Accept them?
Friday evening the dashboard shows your KPI 2% short. The month closes after the weekend. You could close the gap on Saturday. Work?
At home you discover your badge went through the wash with your jeans. Meeting at 8 tomorrow; the badge office opens at 9. What do you do?
right: Ask a colleague to meet you

text: At night the portal reminds you: "You haven't confirmed reading the revised Code of Ethics." It's 112 pages. Confirm without reading?
At 8 p.m. Compliance says yesterday's lunch with a client needed prior approval. Lunch was a 350-ruble shawarma. Write an explanation?
right: Call and laugh it off together

text: Friday, 6:55 p.m. Email: "As of Monday, you're moving to a new directorate." Details on Monday. Weekend ruined?
In the evening your kid draws you a "family values poster": "Hugs. Pizza. Parent home by six." Hang it at work?
right: Hang it at home, front and center

text: You run for the last company shuttle; security is checking badges at the door. Yours is stuck in your bag. The driver starts the engine. What do you do?
right: Let it go, take the subway

text: An acquaintance offers you an evening side gig consulting for a small firm. The ethics code requires approval for any outside work. Get approval?
In the evening, the chats of three merged departments become one: 900 people, and someone's already wishing everyone's cat a happy birthday. Stay?
In the morning a new line appears on your sign-off sheet: "Approval Approval Office." It didn't exist before. It's run by your former intern. Call him?
New KPI: "Time to first email reply." To boost it, colleagues answer everything within 30 seconds with "Got it, will look." Join in?
The canteen now requires lunch pre-orders via the portal by 9 a.m. You forgot, so you get the "default lunch" — plain buckwheat. Ask a colleague to share?
left: Beg a cutlet off a colleague

text: You've been assigned the "Conflict of Interest" course for liking a colleague's post about his new business. Take it?
In the elevator, the lawyer who reviews your emails admits: "If you write 'preliminary,' I pass it unread." Use the magic word?
The town hall moved to lunchtime "so as not to disrupt work." Sandwiches promised, but not enough for everyone. What do you do?
Your badge doesn't open the zone with the water cooler. You have to ask colleagues. It's the third time today you've asked the same person. Awkward?
The Forms team unveils the "simplified request form": 12 fields instead of 14, but each must now be approved separately. Speak up at the presentation?
The morning shuttle from the subway to campus is packed. The driver says: "One more fits." Next to you stands a colleague on crutches. Let him go?
left: Let him on, wait for the next

text: The corporate campus has 14 buildings. Your meeting moved from Building A to Building M ten minutes before start. They're 1.5 km apart. Run?
right: Join by video from Building A

text: 8:05 a.m. 211 unread emails, 180 of which are mass mailings you're cc'd on. There's a "Mark all as read" button. Press it?
right: Go through them one by one

text: At the coffee machine a colleague catches you and starts recounting his weekend. In detail. Your coffee hasn't poured yet; call in 4 minutes. Listen?
A new person sits at the next desk this morning — here for a week under hot-desking. He's quiet and clearly shy. Introduce yourself?
Morning traffic jam at the campus gate: the barrier scans plates one by one. You've been waiting 25 minutes. Abandon the car and walk?
right: Wait and take calls from the car

text: At the morning stand-up the manager asks for "one piece of good news" from each person. Yours: you found matching socks. Share?
The intern is an hour late: "Badge doesn't work, security won't let me in." You're his mentor. Go down for him?
right: Send him to the badge office

text: 8:20 a.m. A client says yesterday's delivery went to the wrong place. Logistics starts at 10. You know the warehouse, but it's not your area. Call?
At rush hour, elevators to your 38th floor come every 15 minutes. Colleagues start a "stairs club" to climb together. Join?
right: Wait for the elevator with a book

text: Monday, 8 a.m. The CEO sends a 12-minute video, "Onward to the New Week!" Viewing is tracked. Watch it?
right: Watch with the team over coffee

text: At 8:15 a colleague calls: "I'm sick, and I'm presenting to the board at 9. Can you save me?" You've barely seen his deck. Take it?
The receptionist greets you by name every morning. Today she's crying: she's being moved to another building. Stop and talk?
You arrive at 7:30 to work in peace, but the open space is mid-deep-clean, vacuums roaring. What do you do?
You learn your boss has gone on vacation and named you "acting head." He announced it in his auto-reply. Take over?
Your team lunches together once a month, and today's the day. But a VP just invited you to a "working lunch." Which?
A colleague in the next group made an error in a report, and management noticed. He doesn't know yet. Warn him?
You've been named floor warden: check that coffee machines are off and windows closed. You leave last anyway. Agree?
A colleague from another team can't submit his report: his spreadsheet broke and he's panicking. You can fix it, but it'll take an hour. Help?
Pizza is ordered for a long meeting. Three boxes, twenty people. You're closest to the door when it arrives. What do you do?
right: Take a slice, pass it on

text: Someone accidentally posts in team chat: "There goes [boss's name] with his ideas again." The boss is in the chat. It's been up for 30 seconds. What do you do?
A colleague is collecting donations for an orphanage and asks for help delivering boxes after work. You promised yourself to leave on time. Help?
At the water cooler, colleagues discuss the new director and want your take — you worked with him before. He was a good boss. Say so?
A colleague texts at 8 p.m.: "Could you proofread my text? It's for the idea contest, due at midnight." Two pages. Do it?
right: Wish her luck, go to bed

text: After work a colleague invites you to the gym — "it's more fun together." You've been meaning to start, but you're tired. Go?
On the evening subway you see a colleague you've never spoken to in five years on the same floor. He nods at you. Start a conversation?
In the evening you remember a colleague bailed you out last week and you never thanked him. It's late. Write now?
Inventory check. Your monitor has no asset tag, and the database lists a monitor under your name you've never seen. What do you do?
You spent a week on an urgent task, but there's no project code for it in the timesheet system. Without one, the hours don't count. What do you log?
right: Request a new code via committee

text: You're editing a shared document with 14 others at the same time. Your paragraph vanishes for the third time. What do you do?
right: Agree on an order in chat

text: Email blocks attachments over 10 MB. Your client deck is 46 MB. File-sharing sites are blocked. How do you send it?
right: Deliver it on a flash drive

text: Your boss's boss invites you to a skip-level meeting and asks how it's going with your manager. Be honest?
The company declared "No-Meeting Wednesdays." Now all meetings have moved to Tuesday, booked solid 8 to 8. Propose something?
The new director wants a daily status report from everyone at 5 p.m. It takes 40 minutes. You spend more time reporting than working. What do you do?
Real Estate now bills your department for every meeting room booked. Your budget's melting. The team starts meeting in the stairwell. Go along?
The mentoring program assigned you a mentor. He's ten years younger and opens with "stop being afraid of AI." Continue?
The company opened an "innovation lab" with beanbags and neon. Nobody goes, since entry is by request. Go work there?
The new corporate font is mandatory, but it's not installed on your PC. IT takes a week. The document's due today. What do you do?
right: Ask a colleague to export a PDF

text: The new deck template requires a 4-line disclaimer at the bottom of every slide. Your tables run to the bottom edge. What gets cut?
right: Put the disclaimer on the last slide

text: To sign a client contract, you need a power of attorney. Legal won't issue one without seeing the contract. Full circle. What do you do?
left: Get Legal and the client in one room

text: At the engagement survey readout, your team ranks last. The director wants an "action plan by Friday." Your team looks at you. What do you propose?
The "engagement plan" introduces mandatory "Fun Fridays," 4 to 6 p.m.: board games, contests, a photo report. The team groans. How do you run it?
At the strategy session you're assigned the role of "devil's advocate" — criticize everything. By lunch, every department is offended. Keep going?
Legal requires initials on every page of the contract in triplicate. 140 pages. The client is waiting in the meeting room. Sign in front of him?
left: Sign in front of the client

text: A branch courier is bringing the originals by train. It's four hours late; signing is at 4 p.m. What do you do?
left: Sign on scans with a guarantee

text: Eco policy made double-sided printing the default. The client got a contract with your signatures on the backs of the wrong pages. Reprint?
Your meeting is in room "14.3.C.27-bis." No one on the floor knows where that is. Five minutes to go. What do you do?
right: Hold it by the nearest window

text: HR asks you to name "two successors" for your role. If you name strong ones, you might be replaced. Who do you name?
The portal awards points for posts and likes. A colleague earned 40,000 posting values memes. Points convert to mugs. Start posting?
The company is selling old office furniture to staff for a token price. Your beloved armchair is on the block. Bid?
right: Let a colleague who wants it win

text: In the evening the time system shows 46 hours of overtime this month. Compensation needs sign-off from three managers. File for it?
At 9:30 p.m. you realize you've eaten nothing but meeting cookies all day. The fridge at home is empty. Order in or walk to the store?
right: Order in and finish the report

text: The mandatory evening webinar "Preventing Burnout" runs three hours from 7 p.m. Webinars like this are exactly what's burning you out. Attend?
You go to bed at 11, but your brain keeps routing tomorrow's document through twelve departments. It's 1 a.m. What do you do?
left: Get up and write it all down

text: After 8 p.m. security won't let food delivery in. You're on the 41st floor. Go down?
right: Ask security to bring it up

text: Your desk neighbor leaves at 6 every day looking happy. You leave at 9 looking like he does on Mondays. Ask his secret?
The company pays for taxis after 10 p.m. It's 9:45. Stay 15 more minutes for a free ride?
Your partner says, "First time home before eight all week." It should sound like good news, but it sounds sad. How do you respond?
You planned an evening run, but a VP sent a "small request" — an hour's work. Run or request?
You're on overnight system duty for a week. Phone on 24/7. First night: three false alarms. What do you do?
Tonight: laundry, homework with your kid and 40 unread emails. You have energy for one. Which?
The power's out at home tonight. Laptop dead, phone at 9%. The report is due in the morning. What do you do?
A friend asks for help moving on Saturday. Saturday's your "voluntary" ERP go-live shift. Your answer?
The elevators were shut off tonight "to save energy." Only the freight elevator runs. You're on 33. Wait or walk?
You set a 5:30 a.m. alarm for an Asia call. You could ask a colleague from another team to cover. Ask?
You want to watch a series tonight, but work chat has 76 new messages. Show or chat?
In the evening they announce your department moves to a new out-of-town campus on Monday. Ninety minutes each way. What do you do?
left: Look for jobs closer to home

text: The corporate running club meets at 6:30 by the campus entrance. A VP runs too — a chance to talk outside meetings. Get up?
Third meeting in a row, and the vending machine has only a "Tropical Storm" energy drink left. Drink it?
After last night's crunch till midnight, you're in at 9. Colleagues who left at six are chipper. The boss thanks everyone equally. Hurt?
You slept four hours. Budget defense before the finance committee at 9. You have 20 minutes. Review the numbers or nap in the car?
The wellbeing program offers yoga at 8 a.m. and 1 p.m. You signed up for morning but you're running late. Switching to lunch means skipping lunch. Which?
You finally got a sit-stand desk. It goes up but won't come down — broken. Repair needs a ticket. Work standing all day?
Your company wristband reminds you every half hour to "drink water." The floor's cooler has been empty since Monday. What do you do?
8:10 a.m. In team chat: "Can anyone cover my 9 a.m. call with the region? My kid has a fever." Silence. You?
right: Stay quiet, you have your own

text: A colleague from a dissolved department joins your team this morning. No laptop, no badge, no chair. Share yours?
right: Send him to IT and Facilities

text: In the elevator line, a colleague whose email you never answered a year ago waves at you, smiling. Go apologize?
The team learns its beloved Friday donut stand-up was cancelled "for optimization." They suggest holding it unofficially. Are you in?
After two teams merge, someone must own the shared task tracker. Your colleague and the former rival both want it. Yours is the deciding vote. Who?
Colleagues chipped in for coffee for the whole team and forgot to include you. The courier's standing there with the tray. Say something?
The intern brings an idea that would save the team two hours a day. Implementing it needs three departments' sign-off. Champion it?
A colleague asks to swap seats: she has the AC blasting behind her, you have the window. You love your window. Swap?
A colleague admits he botched a task you co-own. The boss doesn't know yet. Meeting at 10. What do you do?
Every morning a colleague watches videos without headphones. You've endured it for three weeks. Today it's a video on how to be calmer. Say something?
A colleague asks you to glance at his report before it goes to the CEO. You spot an error on page one. Fifteen minutes to send. Speak up?
left: Point it out and help fix it

text: You discover you're on duty three of five New Year holiday days. Colleagues without kids — none. Push back?
You're paired on a project with the team that blew your deadline last year. Their rep shows up with chocolates to make peace. Accept?
A colleague proposes Friday lunches with people from other departments — "to escape our bubble." Forty minutes. Join?
A colleague was passed over for promotion for the third time. She's sitting quietly, not answering messages. Go to her?
The boss offers you alone a bonus for a project the whole team did. The team won't find out. What do you do?
left: Ask to split it with everyone

text: A new hire accidentally deleted the team's shared folder. IT can restore it, but then everyone will know who did it. What do you do?
The next team keeps tossing you tasks marked "you know this better." Today, the fifth. Push back?
left: Send it back with an explanation

text: A colleague admits he can't handle his workload and fears telling the boss. You could take one of his tasks. Do you?
A colleague from another team is getting married. Money's being collected for a gift, but you don't know her. 1,500 rubles. Chip in?
left: Chip in and sign the card

text: A colleague asks for honest feedback on his talk. It was boring. What do you say?
At 7:30 p.m. the boss wants a report by morning. A colleague offers to split it so you're both done by nine. You could do it alone by midnight. Split it?
In the evening you find a colleague's error that'll send a client wrong numbers tomorrow. He's asleep. Fix it yourself?
The boss texts at 10: "You up? I have an idea." Reply, and it's another hour of chat. Don't, and he's hurt tomorrow. Respond?
The team proposes moving the weekly call from morning to evening, "since mornings are busy." Evenings are your family time. Your vote?
In the managers' chat tonight, they argue whose team to blame for missed deadlines. You know it's the system. Speak up?
Tonight's the farewell for your boss, who's moving to another city. You argued all year, but he taught you a lot. Go?
For the third evening running a colleague stays late and asks you not to leave — "it's creepy alone on the floor." You want to go home. What do you do?
At 1 a.m. a colleague posts in work chat: "Anyone know how to unsend an email to the CEO?" You know — you can't. Reply?
A colleague asks to swap days off: you take Monday, he takes Friday. You'd planned a trip on Friday. Swap?
In the evening elevator the CEO asks why you're here so late. The honest answer: "Because of your new policies." Say it?
The team is pulling an all-nighter for a launch. No food budget. Buy everyone pizza out of your own pocket?
A VP praises you in an all-hands email for a project. Half the work was a colleague's, and he isn't mentioned. Reply all?
A former colleague laid off in the reorg calls asking for a reference. Your boss said "stay out of it." Help?
An overnight release of the new system. Your team is on watch, and you're the lead. Everything's under control — you could leave. Stay with them?
In the evening you hear your team was the department's best this quarter. The boss wants you to pick one person for an award. Whom?
In the evening you type a long message to the boss saying the team is overloaded. Your finger hovers over Send. Now or in the morning?
A colleague asks if he should apply for an internal opening in another department. If he leaves, you'll have more work. Your advice?
left: Go for it if you want

text: The key to the safe with the department seal is with a colleague on sick leave. A document needs stamping by 10. Drive to his place?
The boss is in a foul mood and snaps at a junior in front of everyone. He walks out in tears. What do you do?
right: Wait, then talk to the boss

text: In the department newsletter you spot a colleague's article with whole paragraphs from your report last year. Only his name. What do you do?
A chocolate bar on your desk with a note: "Thanks for bailing me out yesterday." No name. You helped three people. How to find out?
"Italian Day" in the canteen: pasta's gone by 12:15, only "Italian" cottage cheese pancakes left. Your team arrives at 12:20, glum. What do you do?
left: Take everyone to a café nearby

text: At the salad bar, a Finance colleague scoops up all the avocado. Twenty people behind him. Say something?
The canteen now fines unreturned trays, with cameras on every table. Your boss left his tray behind. Return it for him?
The staff store sells company products at a discount. A colleague asks you to buy ten in your name for his relatives. Limit: five per person. Help?
You search the portal for a contract template. Results: 2017 party photos, the canteen menu and an order about improving portal search. What do you do?
right: Dig an old one out of email

text: Company cars must be booked three days ahead. You need to reach a client in an hour. Only the VP's car is free, with a bored driver. Ask him?
The archive is being digitized; you're asked to check 4,000 scans "for legibility." The schedule says "1 hour." What do you do?
A regulator sent a request due in 48 hours. The data sits in six systems; you can't access four. Whom do you call first?
You got a paper cut. Health & Safety requires a workplace injury report with three witnesses. There were none. What now?
You've been named floor fire warden: orange vest, whistle and Saturday training. Opting out needs a doctor's note. Accept?
right: Pass it to an eager colleague

text: Security asks you to remove a photo of the office kitchen from your personal page: a screen with a chart is visible. The chart shows canteen pie sales. Delete it?
A vendor demos his system, and it crashes three minutes in. He asks for "ten more minutes." You have another meeting. Give him the time?
A regional director visits HQ and asks you to show him "how things work here." He knows his job well and nothing about yours. How much time do you give?
right: An hour and a reading pack

text: You sent a mailing to 3,000 clients, and every greeting reads "Dear {FirstName}." Marketing is already calling. What do you do?
You're hosting a webinar for 2,000 employees. A minute before start, your mic only transmits a whisper. Begin?
Corporate health insurance won't cover your appointment: the clinic is "not in the plan." This year's plan includes one clinic, across town. Take it up with HR?
Your boss leaves you signing authority for a month. On day one, a contract arrives for an alarming sum. Sign?
A meeting runs noon to 2 p.m. "with lunch." Lunch is crackers and mineral water. You skipped breakfast. Step out for food?
A colleague from the Asia office is in Moscow for the first time and too shy to ask where the canteen is. Day two, he's eating only cookies. Invite him along?
left: Take him and show him around

text: Your canteen card didn't top up due to a "payroll module glitch." A colleague offers to buy your lunch on her card. Accept?
left: Accept, pay her back in cash
right: Go buy food at a shop

text: 8 a.m. New order on the portal: "As of today, all memos are written in the third person." Your "I request a monitor" memo is already out for signature. Rewrite it?
The badge office installed a ticket machine: you get a number by tapping your badge. Yours is broken — that's why you're here. What do you do?
First day back from vacation. 1,400 emails and five meetings you know nothing about. Where do you start?
This morning your card stopped opening your office, but your officemate's still works. He's not in yet. Wait for him in the hall?
8:30 a.m. mandatory webinar: "New Travel Approval Policy." Ten minutes in, the speaker says, "Now let's go back to the old one." Keep watching?
The boss gets the turnstile report and asks why you arrived at 9:07 yesterday. You were in the turnstile line from 8:30. Explain?
right: Offer to check the line together

text: An auditor arrives at 8:45 asking for "evidence you've read the policy." You did, but what counts as evidence? What do you show?
right: Show your signature on the log

text: Your team is split across two campus buildings. Morning meeting in Building B; your laptop is in Building G. The shuttle runs every 20 minutes. What do you do?
19 voicemails on your work phone this morning. Listening requires a PIN you never set. Call IT?
Your temporary badge expires at 9, and the permanent one is "next week." The guard offers a new temp pass each day. Twenty minutes each. Agree?
right: Talk him into a week's extension

text: You learn the quarterly plan was approved without you. Your project is in it — two months earlier than planned. What do you do?
left: Go to the boss with a timeline
right: Rally the team and speed up

text: You arrive first at 7:50, and the floor alarm goes off: the system flags you as an "after-hours intruder." Security is running your way. What do you do?
right: Retreat to a café till nine

text: Culture hands out free breakfast "for engagement" to anyone who checks in on the app. Your phone's dead. A colleague offers to check you in. Accept?
Risk sends a "heat map" with your project glowing red. Reason: "missing risk report." You submitted it a week ago. What do you do?
A colleague who lives next door drives in daily and offers you a lift for half the gas. But he leaves at 7 a.m. Accept?
The meeting room got a new control panel: 40 buttons on a touchscreen. You just need the projector on. Guests have arrived. What do you do?
right: Call IT and entertain the guests

text: At 8:20 you learn there's a photo shoot for the annual report today, and you're in it. You're in an old T-shirt. A colleague offers her shirt. Take it?
A courier with partner documents needs a signature from "director level or above." The director's in after lunch; the courier leaves in ten minutes. What do you do?
At the evening retrospective the team writes "what went wrong" stickies. Half say "approvals." Take that upstairs?
In the evening you realize you left the flash drive with tomorrow's deck in a taxi. A colleague has a copy, but he's off to his country house with no signal. What do you do?
In the evening the team surprises you with a cake: one year since you became their lead. You'd planned to leave early. Stay for tea?
In the evening a colleague asks you to sign off his report as "reviewer," though you haven't seen it. "It's fine, honestly." Sign?
Colleagues from the Siberian branch call at 9 p.m. your time — it's morning there, and they need help with a document. No one else to ask. Answer?
In the evening a gossip chat claims your colleague is being fired. You know it's false. Set them straight?
The boss invites the team to a company-paid dinner — at 9 p.m., after all meetings. Half the team has kids. Suggest moving it?
Teammates are hauling boxes to the new floor this evening — Facilities provided no movers. You've got your coat on. Help?
left: Take off the coat and help

text: Your next-door neighbor works in your department. At 10 p.m. he knocks with his laptop: "Help me with this report, please?" Open the door?
A colleague posts a parody of the company anthem in work chat. Everyone's laughing, but the deputy director is in the chat. React?
A colleague texts that there's trouble at home and he needs a couple of unpaid days. The boss is on vacation; you're acting head. Let him go?
right: Tell him to wait for the boss

text: A client turns up at reception at 7:40 p.m. unannounced, demanding "the project lead." That's you, and you were heading out. Go down?
At dinner your daughter asks why you always say "let's sync" instead of "let's talk." The family awaits an answer. Your response?
A long-retired former colleague calls in the evening: he misses the place and wants company news. It could take an hour. Answer?
right: Promise to call on the weekend

text: The night before the town hall the boss asks you to prepare an "awkward question" he'll "spontaneously" ask the CEO. It's about your team. Do it?
You found free evening courses for your team, but HR says training must be on work time — and there's no time during work. What do you do?
At 11:30 p.m. one of your people emails his resignation, subject: "Please understand." You had no idea he was struggling. Call now?
Friday evening the boss announces a "voluntary workday" on Saturday. No volunteers. He looks at you. Step up?
Morning directive: "All decks — 5 slides max." Yours for the board is 38 slides, showing at 11. What do you do?
The night support agent hands you 14 unresolved tickets marked "very angry." Your shift hasn't started. Take them?
You're late because of a highway accident. The boss requires a written memo for any lateness. First time in two years. Write it?
In the morning you're asked to translate the CEO's letter for the overseas office into English — "you studied it, right?" The translators are on leave. Take it?
At 8:30 HR asks each manager to name "one employee you're proud of" for the honor board. You have five worthy people. Who?
left: Name one, praise the rest privately

text: Twenty new chairs arrive for your team this morning, with assembly instructions in a language no one reads. The movers are gone. Build them?
A client calls at 8: "Your new contract is 70 pages; the last one was three. What changed?" Only the legal team changed. Your answer?
Culture asks each department for a wall newspaper for the company's anniversary. Due Friday. No artists on the team. Who draws?
You find three versions of the same policy in circulation: on the portal, in email and on the wall. They contradict each other. Which do you follow?
At the stand-up you're handed the "Best Department" rotating trophy. It must be displayed and dusted per policy. It weighs 6 kg. Where does it go?
A delegation from another corporation arrives to "learn from your experience." The boss asks you to give the tour. Your experience: twelve sign-offs. What do you show?
The guest Wi-Fi password changes every morning, available only from the ground-floor guards. Your guests on 30 are waiting. Run down?
Comms is shooting an internal web series about office life and wants you for a cameo as "the weary approver." Shoot's at lunch. Agree?
A document between the Moscow and St. Petersburg offices takes two weeks by internal mail, two days by regular post. Policy says internal. How do you send it?
After each client meeting you must fill in a 30-field CRM report. You had seven meetings. Fill them all today?
Hot-desking puts you at a desk with someone's family photo and a "Best Dad" mug. Clearly someone thinks it's his. Move?
The new director introduces standing meetings "to keep them short." This one runs two hours, everyone on their feet. Your back hurts. What do you do?
You were accidentally paid double this month. Accounting hasn't noticed. A colleague says "wait, maybe they won't." What do you do?
Security randomly screens email. You're notified that your message with the word "bomb" ("this deck is the bomb!") is under review. Explain yourself?
You accidentally join a closed leadership call — the link was in a shared calendar. They're discussing the reorg. No one's noticed you. What do you do?
The night before the annual report, a colleague admits he lost half the data. Two of you could rebuild it overnight. Stay?
From the 45th floor you watch the city lights and realize your last walk through it was in summer. It's November. Go for a walk?
You learn a colleague teaches evening courses using your team's shared materials, without mentioning the company. What do you do?
At midnight you remember you didn't cc Legal on an important email. That's a policy breach. Send "forwarding a copy" now?
right: In the morning, with an explanation

text: The evening train home is your only reading time. Today a colleague sits beside you to "go over a few things." An hour's ride. What do you do?
You submit the annual report at 8:55 p.m., five minutes before the deadline. At 8:58: "Report rejected: invalid date format." What do you do?
In the evening you fill out an anonymous survey with everything you think about management. Finger over Send. Anonymity "guaranteed." Send?
HR wants next year's vacation schedule by lunch. You have no idea about May, but the system won't accept "not sure yet." What do you enter?
A war breaks out over the AC remote: half the open space is freezing, half is melting. The remote ends up in your hands. What temperature?
Six summer interns are brought to you "for two weeks." No tasks for them, yet the internship report must show "results." What do you do?
left: Invent a team project for them

text: Snow buried the campus overnight; paths between buildings aren't cleared. Your building is 600 meters of drifts away. Meeting in 15 minutes. Trudge?
right: Dial in from the nearest building

text: You must send New Year gifts to 200 clients this morning. Compliance capped them at 500 rubles. Choose between a calendar and a chocolate bar.
It's 29°C in the office; the AC is economizing. The dress code bans shorts. A colleague came in shorts and a blazer. The boss looks at you: "Is he yours?" Your reply?
Your training request is denied: "Course does not match your position." It's exactly your specialty. Appeal?
Security wants you to confirm every morning in the system that you "haven't shared your badge." It takes a minute, but at 8 a.m. What do you do?
In the elevator you meet a bewildered elderly man looking for "the HR office on the third floor, back in 1998." It's meeting rooms now. Help?
The new "productivity monitoring" counts only mouse movement as activity. A colleague brought a mouse jiggler. Use one?
At 8 a.m. you learn from a bulletin that your project has been "successfully completed." It's in full swing. The team is stunned. What do you do?
right: Joke about it and keep going

text: You're asked to do the seating chart for the 300-person New Year party. Two VPs can't sit together. Neither can forty other pairs. Take it on?
At the party, the HR director plays Grandfather Frost and calls you up to recite a poem for a gift. The gift is a planner. Do it?
At the summer corporate festival, you're stationed at your department's booth handing out flyers in the mascot costume. It's 30°C. Agree?
A grateful client sent your team a huge fruit basket. Policy says donate it. The team has already eaten a tangerine each. What do you do?
The party tender went to an agency proposing an "office escape room." So the party happens at your desk. Object?
On Family Day you're asked to give children of employees a tour. One asks, "What do you do here all day?" Answer?
The meeting room is 31°C, the AC's broken, the ticket's been open a week. A client arrives in an hour. What do you do?
left: Move the meeting to a café
right: Buy fans with your own money

text: Marketing hands out mugs with the new logo and asks for the old ones back "for brand disposal." Your old mug has been with you eight years. Hand it in?
A team member brought you a fridge magnet from vacation. The gift policy says declare anything received from subordinates. Declare the magnet?
right: Say thanks and stick it up

text: On the evening of December 30, the boss asks you to "quickly wrap up the year's numbers." Everyone's gone. It's just you. Do it?
Evening blizzard: no taxis, subway jammed. Security offers you the office lounge for the night. Stay?
right: Make your way home on foot

text: After the party a pile of unclaimed gifts sits under the office tree. One has your name, in unfamiliar handwriting. Open it?
You promised the kids you'd decorate the tree tonight, but an email says: "Close 12 acts before year-end." The twelfth needs that twelfth sign-off. What do you do?
The last working evening of the year. The office empties out. On your desk: a to-do list for January. Look now or leave without glancing back?
On a summer evening the team suggests holding the planning session on the rooftop. Security says it's closed, but "if you really must, it can be approved." Go for it?
8:15 a.m. Email is down for the whole floor. IT promises "within an hour." Colleagues gather at your desk because yours somehow works. What do you do?
The business-trip train leaves at 7:10. The corporate taxi is 20 minutes late. Your traveling colleague suggests running for the subway. Run?
The boss asks you to mark who on the team "exceeded targets." Everyone did, but there are bonuses for three. How do you mark it?
left: Mark everyone and fight for it

text: You arrive soaked to the skin. A colleague silently hands you a spare company-logo T-shirt. Meeting in 10 minutes. Put it on?
Security is spot-checking badge photos against faces. Yours shows you ten years ago with different hair. They won't let you in. What now?
8:05 a.m. A colleague calls: "You remember your talk at the department conference today?" You don't. It's in 55 minutes. What do you do?
A coworker shares your full name. This morning you got his disciplinary notice. Forward it to him or to HR?
On the morning call you forgot to mute and said, "Here he goes with his synergy again." The speaker heard. Silence. What do you do?
You need to e-sign 60 documents this morning. The department's single signing token is in a colleague's safe; he arrives at 11. Wait?
right: Call him to come in early

text: The corporate "Run From Burnout" race starts Saturday at 7 a.m. The team signed you up without asking. Backing out lets them down. Run?
A team in another city invites you for a week-long "experience exchange." Your team would be without you mid-project. Go?
You want to publicly thank an IT colleague who saved your project. The portal routes thanks through his manager, who dislikes him. What do you do?
It turns out two departments spent three months on the same task without knowing. One is yours. Merge or compete?
The team introduces a "quiet hour," 2 to 3 p.m., no calls or messages. Ten minutes in, the boss calls with "one tiny question." Answer?
Finance mistakenly credited your project with another team's budget. They haven't noticed. You could really use it. What do you do?
You've just joined the procurement committee. Veterans vote "as usual" without reading. You read it and see a problem. Vote no?
The former smoking area is now an "informal chat zone," where all real decisions get made. You never go there. Start going?
Your matrix bosses want the same report in different formats: one as a table, the other as slides. Same numbers. Make both?
right: Ask them to agree on one

text: Comms is launching a podcast and invites you on: "How to Survive in a Big Company." Live, 40,000 listeners. Go?
In a packed elevator, two people from different teams argue loudly about a project. One is your report, and he's wrong. Step in publicly?
Your team merged with an overseas team; stand-ups are now in English. Half your people go silent. What do you do?
An overseas colleague writes in the evening: "What does 'approve in the working order' mean in your policy?" You don't know either. Reply?
The last shuttle left without you. A colleague offers a lift, though he lives at the other end of town. Accept?
You call home to say you'll be late and hear your kid say, "Again?" The boss wants the report by eight. What do you do?
left: Hand it in as is and go

text: A colleague has been on his feet all day and looks wrecked. You're leaving; he's still at his desk. Offer a lift?
Friday at 7 p.m. you get a task "for Monday morning." You know it can't be done without the weekend. What do you do?
In the 5,000-person chat someone asks if the canteen's open Saturday. 400 people reply "don't know." Post the right answer?
The team asks you to win them remote Fridays. You know management will say no. Try anyway?
In the evening you learn a colleague on vacation never filed his report, due by morning. Do it for him or tell the boss?
In the evening you learn your bonus is bigger than a colleague's who worked harder. It's unfair. Tell the boss?
On your commute you listen to the company podcast "5 Minutes of Strategy." Today it's your boss, presenting your idea as his. What do you do?
right: Gently remind him whose idea it was

text: Every Monday a colleague from the next team books the only big meeting room all day "just in case." Your team has nowhere to plan. What do you do?
The turnstiles broke and are wide open. Security asks everyone to sign a paper log. Line: 200 people. Your call starts in 5 minutes. What do you do?
At the morning review the boss asks who's to blame for the missed deadline. It was another department's approval delay. Name them?
The night-shift colleague left a note on your desk: "Didn't make it, sorry! Please finish, it's 10 minutes." It's an hour. What do you do?
right: Finish it, message her about it

text: The boss asks you to manage the team vacation calendar. Everyone wants August, but policy allows only three people off at once. How do you decide?
left: Draw lots in front of everyone

text: A mandatory "productivity diary" starts today: log what you did every two hours. The boss reads it weekly. How do you fill it in?
You forgot to order a pass for an interview candidate. He's at the turnstile. Processing takes 30 minutes. What do you do?
You find your desk moved to the far end of the floor: "seating optimization." Your stuff's in a box; a new team is in your old spot. What do you do?
Every morning a colleague brews tea for the whole team. Today he's out sick, and everyone stands around an empty kettle. Brew it?
At 8:30 Security arrives for a scheduled "clean desk" inspection. Your desk holds a mountain of papers for today's meeting. Clear it?
You're added to your sixth working group this month. Each meets an hour a week; none has decided anything yet. Decline the new one?
The boss invites you to lunch "just to chat." Midway he asks what the team thinks of him. Be honest?
The portal's org chart mistakenly lists you as your boss's boss. Colleagues joke and bow. Tell HR?
right: Enjoy it for a couple of days

text: The CEO's office calls: urgently find the person who "did something in logistics five years ago." No name. Take it on?
right: Explain there's too little to go on

text: The company rebranded, and the logo must be replaced on all 400 of your documents. One week. Do it by hand or wait for the "automated tool"?
Employees can vote on the new office design: "open space," "open space with plants," or "open space with swings." You want offices. Vote?
A neighboring team is drowning, and their lead asks to borrow two of your people for a week. Yours are busy, but less so. Lend them?
At 10:40 p.m. the department head emails a 50-question "urgent" survey due by morning. Half your team will do it overnight. What do you do?
left: Tell the team "we'll do it tomorrow"
right: Fill it in right now yourself

text: A colleague takes evening classes and asks you to cover his 5:30 exits twice a week. The boss doesn't know. Cover for him?
At 9 p.m. one of your people calls: he accidentally sent a client an internal doc with unflattering comments about that very client. What do you do?
In the evening, team chat erupts over who works the holidays. You're the lead and don't want to either. What do you do?
On a trip you discover the hotel booked at the corporate rate is 40 minutes from the partner's office. There's one next door, 300 rubles pricier. Move?
In the evening you read your team's anonymous feedback on you. One comment is especially harsh. You're fairly sure who wrote it. Confront him?
You're heading to the theater and want to switch off your work phone. Policy says managers must be "reachable until 10 p.m." Switch it off?
At 8 p.m. you realize this is your fifth coffee. You need to sleep by 10 and be up at 6 for a flight. One more?
right: One more, the report won't wait

text: At dinner a neighbor asks how many people report to you. You honestly don't know: since the reorg it's been 4 or 19. What do you say?
right: Check the portal at the table

text: An automated report arrives at night: your "portal engagement" score dropped to zero. You were on vacation. Explain?
right: Log in to the portal right now

text: You're asked to stand in for a colleague at vendor talks: he's stuck in an elevator with the documents. Talks start in 15 minutes. What do you do?
The same person from another department rides the elevator with you every morning. A year of silent nods. Today he speaks: "So, who are you?" Get acquainted?
left: Introduce yourself, invite him for coffee
right: Say your name, look at your phone

text: You come in 30 minutes early to plan the day in peace. Colleagues spot you and start dropping by with questions. Hang a "Do Not Disturb" sign?
For the third day running the intern brings you coffee "just in case." You realize he thinks it's part of his job. What do you do?
right: Accept, reward him with a better task

text: Your chair collapses under you this morning. A new one takes 10 days via Facilities. The next team has an empty chair from someone who left. Take it?
right: Sit on a beanbag and wait

text: You arrive at a 9 a.m. meeting — nobody's there. Ten minutes later it turns out it was moved, but only half got the notice. What do you do?
left: Gather who's here and run it

text: You're back from a trip with a box of local sweets. It serves 12; your team has 30. How do you divide it?
right: Give it to those who helped

text: At 7:30 the boss calls: "Can you be in by eight? The CEO wants the report." You're in pajamas, an hour away. Your answer?
Two of your people ask to be seated far apart. The cause: differing views on open windows. Reseat them?
L&D announces an "Effective Communication" training for the whole department — 900 people in one hall. Only the front rows will hear anything. Go?
right: Sit at the back with your laptop

text: The next team can't figure out the new report form you've already mastered. Their lead asks for a workshop. An hour of your time. Do it?
A task you handed to another department a month ago is back with you after passing through five departments. Unchanged. What do you do?
right: Get all five departments in a room

text: Your team has eaten at their desks three days running for a deadline. As lead, you could call a 30-minute team lunch. The deadline won't move. Do it?
You're offered the lead on a prestigious new project. You'd have to hand your current one, which your team loves, to another manager. Accept?
A VP praises you for a report the intern actually wrote. The intern stands there silently. What do you do?
Renovation starts on your floor: drilling 10 to 5. They offer to move your team into the canteen between meal services. Agree?
You're asked to run the internship program: 30 students, lectures and grading. Leadership will notice. Take it?
Your team and Sales argue in a shared chat over who caused a client complaint. The director wants "a joint view by tonight." How do you proceed?
After the reorg, the best window seat is free. As lead, you could take it. One of your people with a bad back asked for that spot's ergonomic chair. Who gets it?
At 11 p.m. the team celebrates a successful launch in chat and invites you to a "virtual toast." You're nodding off. Join?
right: React with an emoji and sleep

text: In the evening you realize you've ignored a branch colleague for two weeks. He politely reminds you for the fourth time. What do you do?
The boss asks you to help his kid with a school presentation tonight — "you're the slide master." Two hours. Help?
At 7:30 p.m. cleaners start vacuuming right by your desk while you're on a client call. The meeting rooms are locked. What do you do?
right: Take the call in the stairwell

text: Your former intern, now in another department, writes: "Can I get your advice? I'm offered a promotion, but in a team with a bad reputation." Reply?
At 8 p.m. a courier brings materials for tomorrow's event: 300 kits to assemble. The team's gone. Start?
right: Ask the team to come at 8 a.m.

text: A recruiter from an even bigger corporation emails: 90,000 employees and "thirteen sign-offs." Reply?
Colleagues from the volunteer club ask for help sorting donations tonight. You promised yourself a couch evening. Go?
Before bed you notice a colleague's still online writing a report. Tomorrow's her birthday. Tell her to go to sleep?
left: Tell her to go to sleep

text: The interns throw a farewell party and invite you as their mentor. You're tired, but they're hoping you'll come. Go?
At 10 p.m. a colleague finds an error in your document and fixes it himself without telling you. You'd have been embarrassed at the board tomorrow. How do you thank him?
Friday, 7 p.m. You've survived the week: twelve sign-offs, a town hall, two turnstiles and one cutlet. The office empties out. What now?
The guard who lets you out last every night is marking 20 years at the company today. No one has congratulated him. What do you do?
In the evening you reread your list of goals for the year and realize half of them begin with "get approval." Time for a change?
In the evening elevator, the cleaner from your floor admits she knows more about the company than any VP: "I read all the drafts people throw away." Ask her more?
In the evening you make yourself a door sign: "Approved by me, with me." Hang it up tomorrow morning?
right: Keep it at home as a souvenir
